summary: The non-GAIA variant is a code-only Python simulation with separate models, monitoring agents, task assignment, truck management, and an operation service. It covers the main domain concepts better than the GAIA prototype, especially container/truck state and fuller-truck prioritization, but it does not implement true autonomous communication and its nearest-truck and timely-removal logic are incomplete. No critical finding was found, but high-severity requirement and error-handling issues mean the system needs revision.

findings.description: Container and truck state monitoring are explicitly modeled.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/agents/system_monitoring_agent.py:13-23 reports total/full/warning/overdue containers and free/busy/full trucks.

findings.description: More-filled trucks are prioritized by load percentage.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:73-77 sorts trucks by current_load / capacity in descending order.

findings.description: Nearest-truck selection is a placeholder and returns the first free truck rather than calculating distance.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:48-56 says actual distances are not calculated and returns free_trucks[0].

findings.description: The one-day timely-removal requirement is only partially checked and does not track how long a container has been full.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:58-71 compares now to last_empty_time only when last_empty_time exists.

findings.description: The system uses direct in-memory method calls instead of defined autonomous container-to-truck or agent-to-agent communication contracts.
The main entrypoint catches broad Exception, prints the error, and returns None, which hides failure semantics from callers.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/main.py:13-20 wraps run_simulation() in except Exception as e and returns None.

findings.description: Dependencies are minimum-version constrained rather than pinned, reducing reproducibility.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/requirements.txt uses entries such as crewai>=0.20.0, pydantic>=2.5.0, and pytest>=7.4.0.

logical_inconsistencies: TaskAssignmentAgent claims to assign the nearest available truck, but the system model explicitly returns the first free truck.
The requirements describe autonomous communication between containers and a truck network, but the implementation coordinates through synchronous in-memory service calls.
implementation_risks: Truck assignment can be geographically wrong because location strings are not used for distance calculation.
Containers with last_empty_time unset may evade the overdue check even when they are full.
Broad exception handling in main.py can hide runtime defects during simulation or integration.
Unpinned dependencies can change behavior across installs.
